# Split service

A small HTTP JSON service for groups of people who share expenses: who paid what, who owes whom. Node.js 24.2 or later, no dependencies.

## Run

```
npm start
```

| Env | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `PORT` | `3000` | Port to listen on (127.0.0.1 only) |
| `DATA_FILE` | `groups.json` | Where the store is kept |

On start it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. A missing data file is an empty store. Every change is written to the data file atomically (temp file, then rename), so a crash never leaves half a file.

## Test

```
npm test
```

## API

| Route | Body | Success | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /groups` | `{id, name, members}` | 201 the group | 400 invalid, 409 `group already exists` |
| `GET /groups/:id` | | 200 `{id, name, members}` | 404 |
| `POST /groups/:id/expenses` | `{description, payer, amount, split?}` | 201 the expense | 400 invalid, 404 unknown group |
| `GET /groups/:id/expenses` | | 200 `{expenses}`, sorted by id | 404 |
| `PATCH /groups/:id/expenses/:expenseId` | any of `{description, payer, amount, split}` | 200 the changed expense | 400 invalid, 404 |
| `DELETE /groups/:id/expenses/:expenseId` | | 204 | 404 |
| `POST /groups/:id/payments` | `{from, to, amount}` | 201 the payment | 400 invalid, 404 unknown group |
| `GET /groups/:id/payments` | | 200 `{payments}`, sorted by id | 404 |
| `GET /groups/:id/balances` | | 200 `{balances}` | 404 |
| `GET /groups/:id/settle-up` | | 200 `{payments}`, suggested, not recorded | 404 |
| `POST /groups/:id/import` | `{entries, dry_run?, skip_recorded?}` | 201 `{expenses, payments, skipped, balances}` (200 with `dry_run`) | 400 invalid, 404 unknown group, 413, 422 `import rejected` |

An expense is shown as `{id, description, payer, amount, split, shares}`, where `shares` maps each name in `split` to what that person's part of the expense is. A payment is `{id, from, to, amount}`: `from` pays `to` back. Expense ids and payment ids each count up from 1 across all groups and are never reused.

**Shares.** An expense is shared equally, in whole cents, by the people in its `split`. When the amount does not divide evenly, the first people in `split` pay one cent more each, so the shares always add up to the amount: 10.00 split between Ann, Ben and Cara is 3.34, 3.33 and 3.33.

**Balances.** `balances` maps every member, in the group's member order, to what the group owes them (positive) or what they owe the group (negative). The payer of an expense is owed its amount, and each person in its `split` owes their share. A payment raises `from`'s balance and lowers `to`'s by its amount. The balances of a group always add up to 0.

**Settling up.** `GET /groups/:id/settle-up` suggests the payments `[{from, to, amount}]` that would bring every balance to 0, without recording them. While someone owes money, the member who owes the most pays the member who is owed the most the smaller of those two amounts; on a tie, the member who comes first in the group's member order goes first.

**Editing.** `PATCH` changes only the fields its body gives, each checked by the same rule as on `POST`; the others keep their value. Shares and balances always follow the expense as it is now.

**Importing.** `POST /groups/:id/import` records a list of expenses and payments for a group in one go: all of them, or none of them. The body is `{"entries": [...], "dry_run": <boolean>, "skip_recorded": <boolean>}`; `dry_run` and `skip_recorded` are false when left out. An entry is an expense `{"type": "expense", description, payer, amount, split?}` or a payment `{"type": "payment", from, to, amount}`, each field checked by the same rule as on `POST`. A field counts as left out only when its key is absent: `null` is checked like any other value. After the 413 and not-an-object checks, the first of these that fails decides the reply, and a failed check saves nothing:

1. Unknown group: 404 `{"error": "not found"}`.
2. 400, first match: `unknown field <name>` (any body field other than `entries`, `dry_run` and `skip_recorded`, first in `Object.keys` order), `entries must be an array of 1 to 50 items`, `dry_run must be true or false`, `skip_recorded must be true or false`.
3. 422 `{"error": "import rejected", "problems": [{"index", "rule"}]}`, one problem per entry that breaks a rule, sorted by index (from 0). `rule` is the first rule the entry breaks, in this order:
   - `not-an-object`: the entry is not a JSON object (null and arrays are not objects).
   - `bad-type`: `type` is not `"expense"` or `"payment"`.

Descriptions are compared after `trim()` and `toLowerCase()`, amounts in cents; `split` is not compared.
   - Payments: `bad-from` (not a member), `bad-to` (not a member, or the same as `from`), `bad-amount`. Payments are never `duplicate` or `already-recorded`.

   With `"skip_recorded": true`, an entry whose first broken rule is `already-recorded` is skipped instead of being a problem.
4. 201 `{expenses, payments, skipped, balances}`: the new expenses and payments in entry order, shown as their `POST` routes show them, with consecutive ids of their own kind in entry order (skipped entries take no id); `skipped`, the indexes of the skipped entries, ascending; `balances`, every member's balance after the import, as `GET /groups/:id/balances` gives it. The import is saved in one write; when every entry is skipped nothing is written.

With `"dry_run": true` every check and error is the same, and a passing import gets the same body with status 200, but nothing is saved: the ids shown are the ones the next expenses and payments will get.

**Rules**
- `id` (group): 1 to 30 characters of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, starting with a letter.
- `name` (group): a non-empty string of at most 100 characters.
- `members`: an array of 2 to 20 different member names. A member name is 1 to 30 characters of `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `_` and `-`, starting with a letter; letter case matters.
- `description`: a non-empty string of at most 200 characters.
- `payer`, `from`, `to`: members of the group; `from` and `to` must differ.
- `amount`: a JSON number from 0.01 to 1000000 with at most 2 decimals, such as `12.5` or `4.35`. It is kept as whole cents and shown back as the same number.
- `split`: optional, a non-empty array of different members of the group. Without it the expense is split between every member, in the group's member order.
- Request bodies are JSON objects of at most 10 KB: a bigger body gets 413, a body that is not a JSON object gets 400. On every route but `POST /groups/:id/import`, unknown fields are ignored.
- Every error is `{"error": "<message>"}`. An unknown route is 404 `{"error": "not found"}`. Fields are checked in the order the table lists them; the first bad one decides the 400 message.

- `server.mjs`: start-up, and the request loop: find the route, read the body, run the handler, save.
- `lib/http.mjs`: body reading, JSON replies, errors.
- `lib/routes.mjs`: route table.
- `lib/groups.mjs`, `lib/expenses.mjs`, `lib/import.mjs`: handlers. Handlers return a new store instead of changing the old one.
- `lib/validate.mjs`: input parsers; they throw `ValidationError` (400).
- `lib/ledger.mjs`: money maths on cents: shares, balances, and how expenses and payments are shown.
- `lib/store.mjs`: loading and atomic saving of the data file.
- `test/`: `node:test` suites; `helpers.mjs` starts the app on a free port with a temp data file.

content.text:
I graded the new import tests and the test additions in the three existing suites. They pass the gate: overall 9/10, no item below 8.

`npm test` passed all 82 tests on one run. I tried to re-run it to check for flaky tests, but that Bash call was denied, so I checked only from reading the code: each test gets its own temp data file and a free port, and no test depends on timing. `git diff test/` shows only additions, so no existing test was weakened. I did not re-run the 37 near-miss copies myself.

**Strengths**
- **Exact assertions:** almost every refusal is checked with `deepEqual` on the whole reply. The shared helpers `assertRefused` and `assertProblems` (in `import-body.test.mjs` and `import-rules.test.mjs`) also check that the data file and the API's view of the group are unchanged afterwards. The checks on whole 201 and 200 replies (`mixedReply`, `import-success.test.mjs:19-27`) cover ids, shares, skipped entries and balances at once.
- **Spec coverage:** every numbered step in the Importing section has tests that would catch a plausible wrong implementation:
  - 404 is checked before body errors.
  - 413 and the not-an-object check apply even for an unknown group.
  - The first unknown field is the first in `Object.keys` order, including integer-like keys and `__proto__`.
  - `null` flags are rejected, not treated as left out.
  - `[ "expense" ]` and `'toString'` give `bad-type`.
  - Description matching tests `trim` against `trimEnd`, so a `trimEnd`-only version fails.
  - A later copy counts as `duplicate` even when the earlier entry is itself `already-recorded` or skipped.
  - `skip_recorded` does not hide other problems, and a rejected import uses up no ids.
  - When every entry is skipped, nothing is written. A dry run shows the ids the next real requests then get, and leaves nothing behind after a restart.
- **Shares and amounts:** `splitEvenly` is tested with the people in a different order and against general properties (parts add up, differ by at most a cent, bigger parts first), so an implementation that gives the extra cent to the last people fails. The `parseAmount` loop over every amount up to 1000.00 rules out `Math.floor` or truncating.
- **Structure:** the four import files are 58–173 lines, each with one theme, and every function is short.

**Minor issues**
- A few places check part of a reply instead of the whole body (`import-body.test.mjs:46`, `:76-77`; `import-rules.test.mjs:21-22`).
- The "raw JSON, then assert 422 and nothing saved" block is repeated twice in `import-rules.test.mjs` (lines 47-51 and 109-114).
- One case in `import-body.test.mjs:63` is a no-op: JSON drops `undefined`, so it only repeats the plain empty-entries check.
- The "10 vs 10.00" case is labelled as testing cents comparison, but both parse to the same number, so it cannot tell cents from raw comparison.
- The spec says an import is saved in one write. The tests check only that a write happened (the file's inode changed), not that it was exactly one.

## GRADE
Overall: 9/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 9 — focused files per spec area, shared fixtures, small helpers that each check status, exact body and nothing-saved
naming: 9 — clear test titles that say what the spec requires; helpers named for intent (assertRefused, assertProblems, seedIds, mixedReply)
duplication: 8 — the raw-text 422 check is repeated twice in import-rules; otherwise well factored
size: 10 — files 58–173 lines, all functions well under 50 lines
errors: 9 — every error reply asserted with an exact deepEqual of the whole body, including precedence (413/not-an-object, then 404, then 400, then 422)
tests: 9 — every Importing/Shares rule covered with cases a wrong implementation would fail; a few success checks look at part of the body; the "one write" rule is not verified
security: 10 — Node built-ins only, temp dirs cleaned up, no secrets
leftovers: 10 — no console.log, debug code or TODOs
